projects.title: Dynamodelx
projects.Description: Dynamodelx is a Python library for creating dynamic machine learning models. It is built on top of Pytorch and provides a simple, quick API's to create and train dynamic models. For more information, visit the GitHub repository.

projects.title: Drafting Agent
projects.Description: Drafting Agent is a Streamlit app that uses Hugging Face Transformers to generate drafts for various drafting tasks between government entities. For more information, visit the Github public repository.

projects.title: Baseline OS
projects.Description: Baseline OS is a Linux distribution built and designed to provide a minimalistic environment to train machine learning models. It is build by customizing arch linux baseline profile. It is designed to be lightweight and fast, with a focus on utilizing the most out of the hardware resources by removing unnecessary packages and services. More Information about the project can be found on the Google Drive folder.

projects.title: Make Sense
projects.Description: Make Sense is a pipeline that converts research paper PDFs into structured, beginner-friendly explainer PDFs. It extracts a paper's text, tables, formulas, and figures, rewrites the content into a clearer explanation using an LLM, and renders the result back into a formatted PDF. For more information, visit the GitHub repository.
projects.Stack: Marker, Pandoc, Tectonic, Gemini API, OpenRouter

projects.title: Shivira Travels
projects.Description: Shivira Travels is a 15-year-old holiday packages booking company based in Hydrabad, Guntur, Vijayawada. From when it was established, it grew it's customer base based on word of mouth and referrals and broadcasted ads on TV and newspapers. I felt they can do better by going digital, so I offered to take Shivira Travels online by creating a website, official emails to expand their reach and make it easier for customers to book packages online. Now it has a user-friendly website that showcases their holiday packages, allows customers to easily browse and contact them.

projects.title: Calorie Vision
projects.Description: Calorie Vision is a web app that uses computer vision to identify food items and estimate their calorie content and nutritional value. For the time being, it's a simple prototype that demonstrates the concept.So, it was only trained on food images containing 5 classes(Bread, Egg, Meat, Noodles, Rice). Currently it's been removed from online platforms. But the code is available in GitHub repository.

blogs.title: At the Core of Every ML Model There Is A Single Estimation Problem
blogs.abstract: Explores the role of point estimation in statistics and machine learning, showing how sample means approximate population parameters, why bias and standard error matter, and how increasing data size brings estimates closer to the true value.

blogs.title: Confidence Is The New Truth
blogs.abstract: Introduces confidence intervals as a way to express uncertainty in estimation, clarifies common misconceptions, and compares three approaches—Normal, Pivotal, and Percentile—showing when each method works best.

blogs.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation: Finding The Optimal Parameter
blogs.abstract: Explains the intuition behind maximum likelihood estimation, why the log-likelihood is used, and how MLE leads to the sample mean in the normal case. Walks through examples, derivations, and shows consistency of the estimator as sample size grows.

blogs.title: A Hands-On Look At Bayesian Inference
blogs.abstract: Introduces Bayesian inference as an alternative to frequentist tools when data is scarce or non-repeatable. Explains Bayes’ theorem with examples, and shows how priors—flat, weak, informative, and robust—interact with likelihood to shape the posterior distribution and handle uncertainty.

blogs.title: Linear Regression Explained: From Theory to Real-World Implementation
blogs.abstract: Builds linear regression from first principles, showing how the conditional expectation E[Y|X] motivates least squares. Derives slope and intercept using both OLS and MLE, connects residuals to likelihood, and explains model assumptions like linearity, normal errors, and homoskedasticity. Uses simulations and real-world data to show fit, inference, and limitations.

blogs.title: Multiple Linear Regression: How Assumptions, Multicollinearity, and Data Shape Your Model’s Performance
blogs.abstract: Extends simple linear regression to multiple predictors using matrix notation. Shows how multicollinearity makes coefficients unstable, why low R sqaure and heteroskedasticity limit inference on small datasets, and how log-transforming targets can stabilize variance. Demonstrates with real datasets that larger samples and less correlated predictors lead to more reliable coefficients and better fit.

blogs.title: Density Function Estimation
blogs.abstract: Explores density estimation starting with histograms and the effect of bin width. Shows how the choice of smoothing changes the shape of the estimated distribution and introduces the bias–variance tradeoff. Uses the Old Faithful dataset to illustrate the method and how confidence bands give a sense of uncertainty in the estimate.

blogs.title: Moving Past Histograms: Smoothing Out Distributions with KDE
blogs.abstract: Introduces kernel density estimation as a smoother alternative to histograms. Explains how kernels work, why bandwidth controls the balance between noise and oversmoothing, and shows common choices like Gaussian, Epanechnikov, and Uniform kernels. Walks through coding KDE by hand, then compares it to built-in implementations from Statsmodels and Seaborn on the Old Faithful dataset.

blogs.title: A Comprehensive Guide On Classification
blogs.abstract: Provides a comprehensive overview of classification algorithms, starting with the Bayesian classifier and its assumptions. Explains how Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) work, their differences, and when to use each. Covers Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, and Support Vector Machines (SVMs), highlighting their strengths, weaknesses.

blogs.title: Bayesian Neural Networks
blogs.abstract: How can we get epistemic and aleatoric uncertainties just by converting from point-estimates to random-variables ?

blogs.title: Stuff I Learned While Building Models — The Notes I Wish I Had Earlier
blogs.abstract: A collection of practical tips and insights I wish I had when I started building machine learning models. Covers topics like maximizing GPU utilization, clamping gradients to prevent exploding, using BatchNorm for faster convergence, efficient modeling techniques, and the benefits of mixed precision training.
